messages:
Maya (support): New escalation from FlowMetrics SRE — case FM-909. They hit /v1/rerank with lots of 5xxs and 504s during a morning batch. They say p95 went from ~80ms to ~4s and observed gateway timeouts. They attached sample and logs.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Thanks. Can you share the exact raw payload they sent and the model/region? Any SDK version info?

Maya (support): Model rwd-re-rank-v2 in us-west-2. SDK v0.9.1. They supplied what they thought was an array but it looks like a newline-delimited string in one field. Sanitized example:

```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model":"rwd-re-rank-v2",
  "queries": ["what's the warranty"],
  "candidates": "doc1\ndoc2\ndoc3\n...\ndoc120"
}
```

Maya (support): Note: candidates is a string with newlines, not an array. Their client lib did join('\n') and didn't set content-type correctly. They also ramped from 20 qps -> 60 qps and had retries x2 w/o jitter.

Priya (eng-sre): Whoa. If the server accepts that and tokenizes the single huge candidate, per-request tokenization could be enormous. Any server logs showing parse behavior?

Maya (support): Customer supplied excerpts:

```
[gateway] 504 GET /v1/rerank -> upstream timed out after 15000ms
[worker] parse_candidates: detected string payload, converting to single candidate (len=234567 chars)
[worker] tokenize_full_candidate took 3200ms
[worker] scoring_loop: n_candidates=1 but tokens=45000 scoring_time=2100ms
[upstream] 502 upstream connection reset
```

Dana (oncall): Interesting edge: their candidate_count in business logic is 120 but our runtime treated it as 1 giant candidate; scoring cost dominated by tokenization and long sequences, not candidate count. That can blow up CPU/memory, cause worker saturation and timeouts. Retries make it worse.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Good catch. Two failure classes: (A) malformed payloads causing worst-case tokenization, (B) large candidate arrays increasing per-request work. Need to check if we validate candidate types at the gateway.

Logan (support): FlowMetrics confirmed SDK bug: v0.9.1 did a naive join when constructing candidates from DB rows. They pushed a fix but still had clients retrying. They rolled back traffic and errors dropped.

Priya (eng-sre): From infra metrics during the window: worker CPU spiked to 95%, p95 worker latency ~3.9s, queue depth peaked at 72. Gateway upstream timeout was 15s and envoy retried once which multiplied the load.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigations:
- Enforce strict input validation at gateway: reject candidate when type != array or when candidate string length > 10000 chars with 400.
- Add a request-size guard: if total payload > 2MB return 413 with guidance.
- Deploy per-tenant burst throttle for rerank and reduce upstream timeout to 8s to fail fast.

Priya (eng-sre): I'll push validation and timeout change now. Enabling tenant throttle for 15m and adding an alert: rerank.p95 > 500ms sustained for 5m.

deploy-bot: Deployed quick changes: rerank.upstream_timeout=8000ms, api.input_validation.candidates_type=array, tenant.rerank_throttle=enabled (15m)

Maya (support): After deploy FlowMetrics reports errors dropped to negligible and p95 returned to ~110ms. They patched their SDK and sent corrected payloads. They still want a postmortem.

Eve (customer-success): Customer is happy with quick response but wants guarantees and SDK fixes so others don't hit the same bug. They also asked for timeline for the validation being permanent.

Jamal (eng-runtime): Long-term fixes:
1) Harden API -- explicitly validate candidate payload type and sizes in the public contract; return clear 400 messages that include remediation steps.
2) Update SDKs to include client-side validators that assert candidates is an array and enforce max candidate size before sending.
3) Optimize tokenization pipeline to stream-tokenize large candidates and abort early if tokens exceed model limits.
4) Add server-side heuristics: if candidates array length looks inconsistent with declared counts (e.g., candidate_count header vs array length), log and reject.

Dana (oncall): Also recommend adding a consumer-side retry policy in our SDK with exponential backoff + jitter and idempotency keys, and update docs for best practices (max candidates 32-64 per request depending on model).

Priya (eng-sre): Follow-ups: run replay tests in staging with malformed payloads to validate validation rules and add metric 'rejected_malformed_candidates' to detect similar issues.

Logan (support): I'll coordinate the customer postmortem and share mitigation steps and SDK patch timeline.

Maya (support): Summary (provisional): root cause = client SDK bug causing newline-joined candidate string -> massive single-candidate tokenization + retry amplification -> worker saturation and 5xx/timeouts. Actions: validation at gateway (deployed), tenant throttle + timeout (deployed), SDK patch (in progress), runtime optimizations (Jamal). Keeping ticket FM-909 open until SDK v0.9.2 shipped and postmortem posted.

Jamal (eng-runtime): I'll prepare the RFC for tokenization streaming and include a quick docs change for candidate type enforcement. Will also add a server log message to surface "candidates not array" with count and sample hash for debugging.

Maya (support): Thanks team. FlowMetrics will wait for SDK v0.9.2 and the postmortem. Closing loop once SDK release and RFC committed. :thumbsup:
